bio:
Tree: 'Marie Dibiase', parents Giovanni P. Dibiasi (b. 1829) + Rosa Siconolfi (b. 1840). Geni names John's wife as Maria Antonia DiBiasi. FS tree GQWT-LLS: born 1870 Italy, died 5 Jul 1935 (Scranton). 1910 census: Marie, 40, mother of 6 children, all 6 living, immigration 1880; 1920 census: Mary, 43, immigration 1892. 1931 license: 'Mary Dibiasa', born Italy. Listed as dead on son Anthony's 1941 marriage license. Her brother (probable) was Domenico Antonio DiBiasi (b. 28 Sep 1856 Guardia, d. 8 Feb 1922 Scranton). Her birth act was not found: the Guardia Nati 1870 register has no index and needs a page-by-page scan (63 images). The 1850-54 Guardia marriage indexes were downloaded in Round 3 (ital/img/mi185x_m*.jpg) but not read, for her parents' marriage. Context: a Francesco De Biasi, 72, was the declarant at her father-in-law Pietro Petriello's death in 1901. A modern Guardia phone directory lists Di Biasi (12); paese.app counts 5 Di Biase arrivals from Guardia 1830-1912.

Son Charles's marriage-license application of August 1934 names his mother as 'Mary', maiden name 'Bibisi' (a clerk's rendering of DiBiasi), born in Italy and living in Scranton ([R4-S1]). This is a third independent record of her maiden name after the 1931 and 1941 licenses, and it shows her alive less than a year before her 5 July 1935 death. The 1940 census of the Bunker Hill Street block shows a widowed Vincenzo DiBiasi, 74, born in Italy, owning no. 1022, three doors from the Petriello house at no. 1028 ([R4-S2]). He was born c.1866, so he is a plausible brother or cousin of Maria Antonia. The two households of DiBiasis at no. 1022 are a lead for her family, not a proven link.

Round 4 searched without result: PA death index 1935, P volume: the PDF file name could not be found (tried P, P-Q, P-R, P-Q-R, O-P, N-O-P, O-P-Q, N-O-P-Q, O-Q, P-S); the 1939 and 1934 volumes resolve, so the 1935 split is named differently; Antenati Guardia Lombardi Nati 1870: blocked (403) in this round

Round 4: her son Charles's 1934 license confirms the maiden name (as 'Bibisi') and shows her alive in 1934; a widowed Vincenzo DiBiasi (b. c.1866) three doors away in 1940 is a sibling candidate. The 1935 death-index volume could not be located.
